existing_roles.title: Director of Product Engineering (NPI
existing_roles.description:
Kauffman Engineering is seeking a highly strategic and hands-on leader to build and scale the product engineering capability across the full lifecycle from customer technical requirements and RFQ support through New Product Introduction (NPI), APQP, PPAP, and launch readiness.

This role provides strategic and operational leadership for Quoting, New Product Launch and other related product and manufacturing engineering activities such as ECN’s and the like. This leadership role ensures engineering execution is disciplined, scalable, and aligned with operational readiness. The Director of Product Engineering plays a critical role in reducing execution risk to NPI programs, improving launch success (Accuracy, Cost, Quality, Speed, Customer Experience), and ensuring the company can support growth without compromising quality, delivery, or margin.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Quoting Engineering

* Ensure technical feasibility, cost assumptions, risks, and manufacturability considerations are incorporated into all quotes.
* Lead a cross-functional team to improve the speed and accuracy of the quoting process through process improvement and technology adoption.
* Ensure accurate engineering input into cost models, BOM assumptions, labor estimates, and tooling requirements.
* Challenge quoting assumptions to identify cost and improvement opportunities in Operations and the Supply Chain.
* Maintain a current view of the capabilities and capacity of each manufacturing site to make informed decisions when allocating quotes and programs.
* Establish a formal feedback loop that brings production and launch performance data back into quoting standards and assumptions.

Product Engineering

* Lead all New Product Introduction (NPI) engineering activities across all plants, including the onboarding of new customers and programs.
* Own NPI on-time delivery (samples, PPAP submissions, and first production run) and program introduction lead time, leading cross-functional teams to build a predictable, fast, and reliable launch process.
* Ensure NPI teams fully execute APQP activities across all phases, including PPAP readiness and launch execution.
* Lead continuous improvement projects that apply a lean, end-to-end approach from quoting through NPI, improving safety, speed to market, quality, delivery, and cost.
* Manage NPI timelines, resource planning (including equipment capacity, tooling, and other resources), and execution to ensure on-time, on-budget launches.
* Review and present NPI status, risks, and readiness to senior management on a regular cadence.
* Drive consistent launch governance, gate reviews, and escalation processes across sites, including confirming that initial production orders are manufacturable.

Process Standardization & Systems Development

* Develop, implement, and maintain standardized engineering processes.
* Reduce reliance on tribal knowledge by establishing repeatable workflows, documentation standards, and control points.
* Improve consistency and quality of engineering outputs across plants and teams.
* Identify and mitigate technical and execution risks early in the product lifecycle.
* Evaluate and adopt better engineering methodologies and tools, and strengthen cross‑functional coordination.

Plant Integration & Cross‑Functional Collaboration

* Act as a key engineering partner to plant leadership to support execution, troubleshooting, and readiness of new program launches.
* Drive alignment between engineering and operations to ensure manufacturability, capacity readiness, and process capability as part of the launch hand-off to the manufacturing sites.
* Support plant teams during launches, ramp‑ups, and significant engineering changes.
* Collaborate with Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and Operations to ensure integrated execution.
* Lead engineering CAPEX planning for new programs and long‑term capacity needs.

Talent Leadership & Capability Building

* Assess current engineering organization structure, skills, and capacity.
* Develop and execute plans to upgrade engineering capability through hiring, development, and role clarity.
* Lead, coach, and develop the engineering team, setting clear expectations and holding team members accountable for results.
* Build a future‑state product engineering organization capable of supporting multiple concurrent launches.
* Promote a culture of accountability, discipline, and continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Electrical, or equivalent preferred); advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum 7–10 years of engineering experience in manufacturing or industrial environments.
* Demonstrated engineering experience in the design and manufacture of wire harness components in a high-mix, low-volume environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams and managing engineering functions, preferably across multiple sites.
* Proven experience with APQP, PPAP, and launch execution in production environments.
* Strong knowledge of Core Tools (APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, MSA).
* Experience driving engineering standardization and process improvement.
* Understanding of material and labor costing, manufacturability, and cost drivers.
* Project management and cross‑functional leadership experience.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, and Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* Strong communication, organizational, and problem‑solving skills.

**Work Environment:**

* This is an Hybrid position at our Reynosa, MX facility.
* Ability and willingness to travel to U.S. and Mexico manufacturing locations (approximately 25–40%) to provide on-site plant support as business needs require.

**Compensation & Benefits**

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $135k-$155k. Actual compensation decisions are dependent on the minimum requirements outlined in the job description, qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, external market conditions, as well as internal equity.

Our company benefits provide full-time employees with a wide variety of benefits to meet the needs of our diverse workforce. We offer the following benefits: health, dental, and vision insurance, prescription drug benefits, flexible spending accounts, voluntary life insurance, AD&D insurance and a healthy incentive credit. We also provide company paid life insurance and short-term and long-term disability insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO and 9 paid holidays. Annual Company Performance Bonus Program based on achievement of annual goals.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

Kauffman is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse workforce, providing equal employment and advancement opportunities to all qualified individuals. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

*This employer participates in the E-Verify program.*

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Are you able to travel to visit and provide support to our Reynosa, Mexico facility?
* Do you have any experience with Arcadia ECAD, Cadonix or Cableteque software? (If yes, or if you have experience with relevant Harness design tools, briefly explain)

Experience:

* Wire Harness Manufacturing: 1 year (Preferred)

Language:

* English and Spanish fluently (Preferred)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

**POSITION Description**

**Manager/Director of Quality**

**Title:** Manager/Director of Quality

**Location:** Rochester, NY

**Company:** EvolvOptic is a leading supplier of precision machined optical blanks. We are shaping the future together with our collaborators and customers. We are growing our capacity and capabilities for blank manufacturing. The same experienced team that made our company a respected leader in our field remains on the frontlines, keeping production humming and delivering an array of high-quality components. We are proud and honored to be a partner to our customers for their optical component needs providing best-value solutions to meet their priorities, including cost, schedule, and assured quality.

The forecast for the future is bright. We are expanding into large, complex optical components by pulling together the right team, the right technology, and the right methods to provide best-value solutions to ground-based and space-based imaging, semiconductor industry, and high energy optics, such as laser fusion and directed energy.

**Position Summary**

The Manager/ Director of Quality is a senior leadership position responsible for developing and executing EvolvOptic's quality strategy and ensuring the highest standards of product quality, measurement integrity, and operational excellence across the organization. Reporting directly to the President, this role provides strategic and technical leadership for quality assurance and compliance.

**Leadership Expectations**

Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, driving a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer satisfaction while enabling EvolvOptic's growth in commercial space, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and scientific optics markets.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute the company's quality strategy aligned with business objectives.
* Provide executive leadership for Quality, Inspection, Calibration and Compliance functions.
* Lead and continuously improve the QMS and all audit activities.
* Establish quality KPIs and drive CAPA, root cause analysis, and operational excellence.
* Lead supplier quality and serve as the senior customer quality interface.
* Support proposals, NPI, program execution, and manufacturing readiness reviews.
* Build and mentor a high-performing Quality organization.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering or scientific discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, metrology, or manufacturing leadership experience.
* 5+ years in a management or director-level leadership role.
* Experience in precision optics, aerospace, defense, semiconductor, or scientific instrumentation preferred.
* Strong knowledge of optical manufacturing, advanced metrology, ISO 9001, AS9100, SPC, MSA, FMEA, and GD&T.

**Key Competencies**

* Technical credibility with engineers and manufacturing teams
* Strong organizational and prioritization skills
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication
* Risk-driven decision making
* Adaptability and comfort with ambiguity

existing_roles.title: Vice President of Operations
existing_roles.description:
Ferrotherm is seeking an experienced and results-driven **Vice President of Operations** to lead and optimize all aspects of manufacturing operations. This executive leadership role is responsible for driving operational excellence, developing organizational capabilities, and supporting the company's continued growth while strengthening strategic customer relationships within the aerospace industry.

The Vice President of Operations will oversee all operational functions, ensuring the consistent delivery of high-quality, airworthy products to aerospace OEM, defense, and turbine engine customers. As a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, this individual will translate strategy into operational execution while delivering results in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability.

The successful candidate will be a strategic leader with a proven track record of building high-performing teams, driving operational excellence, and leading growth initiatives within aerospace or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.

**People Leadership & Culture**

* Lead, mentor, and develop operational leaders across the organization within a union manufacturing environment.
* Foster a culture of accountability, ownership, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Develop succession plans and leadership pipelines for critical operational positions.
* Reinforce Ferrotherm's commitment to safety, quality, integrity, customer focus, and business excellence.
* Create an environment where employees are empowered to identify risks, solve problems, and drive meaningful improvements.

**Executive Operations Leadership**

* Develop and execute operational strategies that support revenue growth, profitability, customer satisfaction, and long-term business objectives.
* Establish operational goals, key performance indicators (KPIs), and accountability systems aligned with company objectives.
* Partner with Sales, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Information Technology, and Human Resources to ensure cross-functional alignment and effective execution.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the President and Executive Leadership Team on operational risk, capacity planning, and capital investment priorities.
* Act as the executive operational liaison for key customers, supporting executive reviews, audits, escalation meetings, and strategic business discussions.

**Manufacturing Operations & Production Execution**

* Provide executive leadership for machining, assembly, heat treatment, special processes, preventative maintenance, and production support functions.
* Drive continuous improvement in safety, quality, throughput, productivity, utilization, and on-time delivery performance.
* Ensure production plans are executed efficiently while maintaining compliance with customer, regulatory, and internal requirements.
* Implement visual management systems, performance metrics, and accountability processes that support operational excellence.
* Lead initiatives to reduce lead times, improve manufacturing flow, eliminate bottlenecks, and expand capacity.
* Ensure operational readiness for production increases, new product introductions (NPI), and strategic program launches.

**Supply Chain & Planning Leadership**

* Oversee purchasing, supplier management, inventory control, logistics, production planning, and scheduling.
* Drive supplier performance improvements focused on quality, delivery, responsiveness, and cost.
* Develop and maintain robust Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning (SIOP) processes to align customer demand with inventory strategy, available capacity, and production resources.
* Lead risk mitigation efforts related to material availability and supplier constraints.
* Ensure inventory strategies support customer delivery requirements while optimizing working capital.

**Quality, Compliance & Aerospace Standards**

* Provide executive leadership and support for the effectiveness of Ferrotherm's Quality Management System in partnership with the Director of Quality.
* Promote a culture where quality is built into processes, not inspected into products.
* Support successful customer, certification, and regulatory audits.
* Ensure operational processes maintain full product traceability, configuration control, and compliance with airworthiness requirements.

**Financial & Business Performance**

* Develop and manage annual operational budgets and capital expenditure plans.
* Drive EBITDA improvement through productivity gains, cost reduction initiatives, and operational efficiency.
* Ensure effective utilization of labor, equipment, inventory, and facility resources.
* Monitor operational financial performance and implement corrective actions as needed.
* Evaluate and justify investments in equipment, automation, facilities, and technology.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including executive-level responsibility.
* Proven experience in aerospace, aviation, defense, turbine engine, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments involving precision machining.
* Strong knowledge of AS9100 Quality Management Systems, aerospace manufacturing standards, root cause corrective action methodologies, and regulatory compliance requirements.
* Demonstrated success leading cross-functional teams, managing organizational change, and delivering measurable business results.
* Strong strategic planning, leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with a Tier 1 or Tier 2 aerospace supplier supporting organizations such as GE Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Safran, Honeywell, Collins Aerospace, Boeing, Airbus, Lockheed Martin, or similar customers.
* MBA or advanced degree in Business, Engineering, Manufacturing, or a related discipline.
* Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other operational excellence certifications are highly desirable.

**Why Join Ferrotherm?**

At Ferrotherm, you'll have the opportunity to make a significant impact on a growing aerospace manufacturing organization. You will help shape operational strategy, lead high-performing teams, and contribute to delivering world-class products to some of the industry's most respected aerospace and defense customers.

If you are a strategic and results-oriented operations executive with a passion for manufacturing excellence, we encourage you to apply.

*Ferrotherm is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.*

Benefits:

* 100% Employer paid Health / Dental / Vision Insurance

You will report directly to our Chief Operating Officer and you'll work out of the Atlanta, GA location on a hybrid schedule.

* Minimum 8 years demonstrated experience in cybersecurity architecture or solution architecture for OT and IT systems.
* Competent with security frameworks and standards such as: ISO 27001, NIST Guidelines, IEC/ISA 62443, CIS.

* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders in a complex, matrixed environment.
Experience leading a high‑impact team 

**Success Measures**

* Understands industry cybersecurity standards and has insights into in country cybersecurity regulations.
* Provides strategic input and guidance for global Buildings OT focused cybersecurity solutions.

Sr. Director, Operational Excellence

**Position Summary**
====================

The Senior Director of Operational Excellence serves as a key strategic and operational partner to the Vice President of Operations, responsible for driving enterprise-wide operational initiatives, workforce optimization, project execution, and organizational effectiveness across CRH Healthcare.

This leader provides direct oversight of the centralized Provider Scheduling team, ensuring effective scheduling operations, proactive coverage planning, workforce utilization, and continuous process improvement. Additionally, the Sr. Director partners with regional and cross-functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, establish accountability, identify operational improvement opportunities, and ensure consistent execution across the organization. The position requires a balance of strategic thinking, hands-on leadership, financial acumen, and the ability to independently drive results in a complex, multi-site healthcare environment.

**Essential Responsibilities**
==============================

**Operational Excellence & Executive Support**
----------------------------------------------

* Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VP of Operations, translating enterprise priorities into actionable execution plans, establishing accountability across functional teams, and ensuring initiatives are delivered on time with measurable operational and financial outcomes.
* Develop and maintain standardized operational performance through reporting that identifies trends, variances, and opportunities across regions. Partner with operational leadership to develop corrective action plans, monitor progress, and ensure sustained improvement.
* Ensure operational excellence with vendors and processes that support the business, including procurement, surveys, and regulatory requirements.
* Support the VP of Operations in evaluating competing priorities, organizational capacity, and resource allocation to ensure alignment with enterprise objectives.
* Develop operational process workflow structure, and communication and training plans to implement, along with feedback loop and tracking to measure success and/or challenge.
* Other duties as assigned by the VP of Operations.

**Workforce Optimization**
--------------------------

* Direct and oversee the centralized Provider Scheduling team, including performance, workload, service expectations and escalation practices.
* Oversee provider scheduling processes, capacity visibility, coverage planning and coordination with regional operational leaders. Identify recurring coverage risks, utilization opportunities and avoidable scheduling disruptions.
* Coordinate with Operational Leadership, Talent Acquisition and Finance on workforce demand, hiring priorities, and labor cost trends.

**Project Management**
----------------------

* Lead full project lifecycle, from planning to closeout for operational initiatives.
* Establish project governance, prioritization, milestones, risks and executive reporting.
* Develop stakeholder engagement, communication, training and adoption plans to sustain operational change.
* Manage project scope, schedules, budgets, and deliverables effectively.

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, operations or related field.
* 7+ years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, workforce management, project delivery or operational excellence.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including demonstrated success leading managers or functional teams multi-stie environment with a distributed field force.
* Experience supporting multi-site healthcare operations; urgent care or ambulatory care experience preferred.
* Proven ability to lead teams, drive change, influence business partners, and deliver operational results through data-driven decision making, stakeholder collaboration, and organizational influence.
* Strong project portfolio governance, change management, workforce analytics, financial acumen and stakeholder influence.
* Ability to lead through partnerships and remote workforce.
* Office based position with approximately 25% travel to company clinics.

*CRH Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of applicable credentialing, licensure verification, background review, and employment requirements.*

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

**Job Description**

The Head of Operational Excellence will lead operational excellence across Shield AI’s Group 3 UAV manufacturing in Frisco, TX (V-BAT) and Group 5 UAV manufacturing in Seattle, WA (X-BAT). Based in Frisco, this leader will create, deploy, and actively manage manufacturing KPIs and performance systems across both sites, embedding operating rhythms that improve accountability, visibility, and results. 
 
You will be responsible for instilling a culture of execution excellence, embedding structured problem-solving practices, and delivering measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and productivity. This includes leading the development and governance of operational standards—such as visual management, 5S, and root cause analysis—while owning the manufacturing budget cycle, business rhythm, and executive reporting interface across both locations. This role partners with engineering, production, quality, and business functions to execute high-priority improvement initiatives, support V-BAT production, and establish operational excellence as X-BAT progresses through prototype and into rate production.

**Do you have the expertise and leadership to embed excellence into the fabric of autonomous defense manufacturing?**

### **What You'll Do:**

* Create, deploy, and actively manage consistent manufacturing KPIs and performance dashboards across both sites to drive visibility and accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.

* Define, train, deploy, and continually improve operational standards across V-BAT manufacturing in Frisco and X-BAT manufacturing in Seattle, including 5S, root cause analysis, and visual management.

* Develop and institutionalize the manufacturing budget process across both sites, including forecasting, controls, and performance tracking.

* Set financial targets in collaboration with operations and finance teams and drive adherence to budget and cost goals.

* Lead high-impact cross-functional improvement initiatives across both sites to improve quality, delivery, efficiency, productivity, and cost performance.

* Prepare and coordinate senior and executive-level reporting packages for Manufacturing leadership reviews.

* Partner with production, quality, and engineering teams to deploy Lean and continuous improvement practices, adapting execution to the needs of established production and prototype-to-rate manufacturing.

* Own business office functions for Manufacturing across both sites, including goal tracking, KPI dashboards, and process governance.

* Coach and train teams and leaders across both sites to elevate operational discipline, share effective practices, and sustain improvements.

### **Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, or related field.

* Experience leading operational excellence, Lean, or business office programs within a manufacturing environment, with the ability to lead improvement across multiple sites.

* Demonstrated ability to design, roll out, and sustain structured operational standards and improvement systems.

* Strong background in budgeting, reporting, and performance management at a senior level.

* Excellent communication skills and experience preparing executive-level summaries and presentations.

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree or formal Lean Six Sigma certification.

* Experience in aerospace, defense, or complex hardware manufacturing environments.

* Proficiency with digital tools for KPI visualization, reporting automation, and business process tracking.

* Track record of influencing change across large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and multiple sites.

With one of the highest customer retention rates in the industry – 97% – ImageFIRST is dedicated to improving patient satisfaction and making staff happy with our white glove service!

Check out our company page: https://www.imagefirst.com/company/

**Director, Operational Excellence - CAPEX**
============================================

**Location:** East Coast (Northeast Preferred) 
**Travel:** Approximately 50%

**Position Summary**
--------------------

ImageFIRST is seeking a strategic, hands-on **Director, Operational Excellence** to lead enterprise-wide engineering initiatives, capital project planning, and operational improvement efforts across our national network of healthcare laundry facilities.

This newly created leadership role will serve as a key partner to Operations and the Senior Leadership Team, driving long-term asset strategy, **capital investment planning**, engineering support, and operational sustainability. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing strategic initiatives, leading complex projects, and rolling up their sleeves to solve operational challenges in the field.

This role offers a unique opportunity to build foundational processes that will standardize engineering practices and strengthen operational performance across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Capital Planning & Strategic Investments**

* Identify, prioritize, and develop capital expenditure (Capex) opportunities across the network.
* Build financial justifications, ROI analyses, and business cases for capital investments.
* Present capital recommendations and project proposals to the Senior Leadership Team.
* Partner with Finance and Operations to align capital investments with business strategy and growth objectives.

### **Project Engineering Leadership**

* Lead enterprise engineering projects from concept through implementation.
* Provide technical leadership for facility upgrades, equipment installations, automation initiatives, and operational improvements.
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and with measurable business impact.

### **Engineering Support for Plant Operations**

* Serve as a technical resource for manufacturing and plant leadership across the ImageFIRST network.
* Provide engineering guidance and problem-solving support for facilities requiring operational or technical assistance.
* Partner with General Managers and Operations Leaders to resolve complex equipment and process challenges.

### **Operational Excellence & Strategic Initiatives**

* Lead cross-functional operational improvement initiatives that support network stabilization, sustainability, and long-term operational performance.
* Partner with Operations Leadership to identify opportunities for increased efficiency, standardization, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a trusted resource for high-impact operational projects across the business.

### **Safety Leadership**

* Champion a culture of safety across engineering and operational initiatives.
* Ensure engineering projects and equipment installations meet all applicable safety standards and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Environmental Health & Safety leadership to proactively reduce operational risk.

**Qualifications**
------------------

### **Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, industrial operations, engineering, or capital project management.
* Experience leading multi-site engineering or operational initiatives.
* Proven experience managing capital projects and developing ROI-driven business cases.
* Strong knowledge of asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and reliability.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders at all organizational levels.
* Strong financial acumen with experience presenting recommendations to executive leadership.
* Ability to travel approximately 50%.

### **Preferred**

* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing or industrial facilities.
* Plant management or operations leadership experience.
* Lean Manufacturing, TPM, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement experience.
* Military leadership experience is highly valued, particularly candidates who have transitioned into manufacturing, engineering, or operations leadership roles.
* Experience within healthcare services, industrial laundry, textiles, food manufacturing, consumer products, or other asset-intensive industries.

**Leadership Competencies**
---------------------------

* Strategic thinker with strong operational execution
* Results-oriented and highly accountable
* Excellent communication and executive presentation skills
* Strong analytical and financial decision-making capabilities
* Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across functions
* Comfortable navigating ambiguity and leading enterprise-wide change

existing_roles.title: Director, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is hiring a Director of Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Quality to build and lead the team responsible for the technical relationship with our supplier base, from first sketch through high-volume production, and for the quality systems that ensure everything that arrives at our factories meets spec. This role reports into our VP, Global Supply Chain and brings together two functions that have to move as one: the engineers who industrialize our components and equipment, and the quality systems and team that hold our suppliers accountable once they are producing.

Form's 85% domestically sourced supply chain was built for a battery chemistry with no existing supplier base, which means the industrialization playbook and the quality systems we need are still being written. You will set that standard: rigorous enough to protect a product with a 100-hour duration promise, and practical enough to work with suppliers who are learning our process alongside us. You will fly high enough to set the strategy and the org, and go deep enough to sit in a root cause review when it matters. 
 
*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Lead Form's Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Supplier Quality organization, growing a team of engineers embedded across battery materials, components, and equipment categories.
* Own the end-to-end industrialization journey for direct materials and made-to-spec components, from design-for-manufacturability review and supplier selection through tooling qualification and sustaining production support.
* Build and own Form's supplier quality management system, including PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and SCAR/8D corrective action processes, calibrated for a novel battery chemistry with no legacy supply base to borrow from.
* Set the technical bar for supplier selection and qualification, partnering with Global Supply Managers to ensure our sourcing strategy is backed by suppliers who can deliver on cost, quality, and schedule.
* Own supplier process capability and yield performance, coordinating with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, and Reliability teams to drive root cause analysis and corrective action when issues surface.
* Develop the roadmap and staffing plan for quality systems aligned to relevant standards (e.g., ISO 9001, IATF 16949) at a scale and stage appropriate to where Form is today and where we are headed.
* Represent supplier technical and quality readiness within the Product Development Process, ensuring every component and supplier is qualified ahead of commercial scale.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to align supplier roadmaps with Form's build plan and deployment targets.

### **What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 12+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, quality, or manufacturing engineering, including at least 5 years in a people leadership role building and scaling a team.
* Demonstrated expertise across DFM/DFA, PPAP, APQP, FMEA, SPC, and structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5 Whys).
* Experience building quality and industrialization systems from the ground up, ideally in a hardware, energy, or battery environment without an established supplier base to lean on.
* Strong technical fluency to go deep with engineers and suppliers, paired with the executive presence to represent risk, tradeoffs, and strategy to senior leadership.
* Comfort operating across the full arc from early design concept through high-volume production and sustaining support, with the judgment to know which problems need a system and which need a phone call.

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.* 
 
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

existing_roles.title: Plant Manager III
existing_roles.description:
EnerSys is a global leader in stored energy solutions helping industrial, infrastructure and defense customers address critical power and operational needs. The company delivers integrated solutions that combine energy storage technologies, power electronics, software-enabled intelligence, technical expertise and comprehensive global customer support. EnerSys supports customers across communications networks, data centers, energy infrastructure, material handling, transportation, aerospace and defense — including applications where power continuity is essential. Serving customers in more than 100 countries, EnerSys helps organizations manage energy more reliably, efficiently and intelligently in complex operating environments where uptime, safety and resilience matter.

 

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager will provide overall leadership for the phased development, start-up, ramp-up, and ongoing operation of the new lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Greenville, South Carolina. This is a unique opportunity to build a factory and its organization from the ground up in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment.

The role will evolve through multiple phases of the project, beginning with facility construction and operational readiness and progressing through equipment installation and commissioning, production launch, workforce ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale manufacturing operations.

The Plant Manager will be accountable for establishing the operating model, leadership capability, organizational structure, culture, management systems, and performance disciplines required to achieve excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and customer satisfaction.

This leader must bring broad manufacturing expertise in a high-volume, fully automated environment and understand the interdependencies across production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people. The successful candidate will combine strong operational and financial acumen with knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing and a demonstrated ability to build organizations, develop leaders, anticipate workforce needs, and establish strong relationships with employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

**Factory Development, Start-Up & Operational Readiness**

* Provide operational leadership throughout the phased development of the Greenville facility, ensuring manufacturing and operational requirements are incorporated as the factory is constructed, commissioned, launched, and scaled.
* Partner with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, EHS, People & Culture, IT/OT, and other functions to establish comprehensive manufacturing readiness.
* Translate facility and project milestones into executable operational plans covering equipment, processes, workforce, training, materials, systems, safety, quality, and infrastructure.
* Ensure equipment, manufacturing processes, systems, organizational capability, and workforce readiness progress together so that potential gaps are identified and resolved before they impact production.
* Establish the operating systems, standard work, governance, performance metrics, escalation processes, and accountability required to transition successfully from project execution into manufacturing operations.
* Lead the operational transition through equipment installation and commissioning, qualification, production launch, ramp-up, stabilization, and full-scale operations.

**Manufacturing & Operational Leadership**

* Provide end-to-end leadership of plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, employee performance, and overall manufacturing results.
* Maintain a comprehensive understanding of plant operating processes and ensure effective integration across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, and supporting functions.
* Establish a culture of operational excellence, disciplined execution, accountability, continuous improvement, and structured problem solving.
* Establish and continuously evaluate plant KPIs to identify performance gaps, determine root causes, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
* Drive improvement in manufacturing productivity, equipment effectiveness, reliability, throughput, yield, quality, labor efficiency, and operating cost.
* Ensure appropriate manufacturing systems, controls, procedures, and escalation mechanisms are established as production volume and organizational complexity increase.
* Champion Lean manufacturing principles and create a culture in which continuous improvement is embedded throughout the organization.

**Lithium-Ion Cell Manufacturing**

* Provide leadership within a technically complex lithium-ion cell manufacturing environment.
* Apply practical knowledge of cell manufacturing processes, automated manufacturing equipment, process controls, materials, quality requirements, and production risks to operational decision-making.
* Work closely with Cell Engineering, Process Engineering, Quality, EHS, and other technical teams to establish safe, repeatable, high-quality manufacturing processes capable of operating at scale.
* Ensure plant teams understand the relationships among process capability, product quality, yield, throughput, equipment performance, manufacturing cost, and customer requirements.
* Support the effective introduction, industrialization, and scale-up of new manufacturing processes and technologies.

**Financial & Business Leadership**
-----------------------------------

* Own plant operating performance from both an operational and financial perspective.
* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, forecasts, labor plans, productivity targets, capital requirements, and cost-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrate strong understanding of the economic drivers of manufacturing and translate operational performance into financial and business outcomes.
* Partner closely with Finance to understand and manage manufacturing cost, labor, productivity, inventory, scrap, yield, capital utilization, and other key plant performance drivers.
* Evaluate significant operational decisions through both manufacturing and financial lenses, balancing immediate execution requirements with the long-term capability and competitiveness of the plant.
* Establish strong cost-management and financial disciplines as the facility transitions from construction and start-up investment to sustainable manufacturing operations.

**Workforce Planning & Organizational Capability**

* Build the plant organization in phases aligned with facility construction, commissioning, production launch, ramp-up, and future operating requirements.
* Develop short- and long-term workforce plans to ensure the plant has the appropriate leadership, technical, skilled-trades, professional, and manufacturing capabilities required at each stage of growth.
* Anticipate talent, capacity, skill, and leadership gaps before they become constraints to manufacturing performance or future growth.
* Partner closely with People & Culture to develop recruiting, workforce planning, onboarding, training, retention, employee engagement, talent management, and organizational capability strategies.
* Establish clear organizational structures, decision rights, accountabilities, and leadership responsibilities as the facility grows and becomes operational.
* Develop workforce flexibility and organizational depth to mitigate single points of dependency and ensure business continuity.
* Regularly assess whether workforce capacity and capability are appropriately aligned with production requirements, operating plans, and future growth.

**Leadership Development & Succession**

* Recruit, build, coach, and develop a high-performing plant leadership team capable of successfully operating at increasing levels of scale and complexity.
* Establish a leadership culture where leaders are expected not only to deliver results but also to develop other leaders and build capability within their organizations.
* Partner with People & Culture to regularly assess leadership capability, organizational effectiveness, succession coverage, bench strength, and future talent requirements.
* Build strong succession pipelines for critical plant leadership and technical positions and ensure appropriate development plans are established for potential successors.
* Identify and develop high-potential talent through coaching, mentoring, expanded responsibilities, cross-functional experience, and targeted development opportunities.
* Establish sufficient leadership and technical depth to minimize organizational vulnerability and ensure continuity as the facility grows.
* Create a culture where talent development and succession planning are ongoing leadership responsibilities rather than periodic HR activities.

**Customer, Supplier & Stakeholder Leadership**
-----------------------------------------------

* Build strong, credible, long-term relationships with customers and ensure plant execution consistently supports quality, delivery, responsiveness, and customer commitments.
* Build strategic relationships with suppliers, equipment manufacturers, contractors, and other external partners critical to the construction, start-up, and ongoing operation of the plant.
* Work collaboratively with customers and suppliers to resolve issues quickly while protecting long-term business relationships.
* Serve as a senior representative of the Greenville operation with business leadership, customers, suppliers, community stakeholders, and other external partners as appropriate.
* Build strong cross-functional relationships across the broader organization and effectively navigate a complex, matrixed environment.
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the plant and foster an employee environment built on communication, engagement, trust, accountability, and strong employee relations.

**Safety, Quality & Culture**

* Establish safety as a foundational operating principle and ensure appropriate systems, behaviors, and leadership accountability are embedded throughout the facility.
* Champion a quality-first mindset and ensure the organization consistently meets internal requirements and customer expectations.
* Build a high-performance culture characterized by accountability, collaboration, transparency, urgency, ownership, and continuous improvement.
* Establish clear expectations for leadership behavior and ensure those expectations cascade throughout the plant organization.
* Create an environment where employees understand how their work contributes to plant performance, customer success, and the broader business.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
* Significant progressive leadership experience within complex, high-volume, highly automated, or advanced manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading a significant manufacturing operation with accountability across safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, people, and financial performance.
* Demonstrated experience supporting or leading the build and start-up of a new manufacturing facility, significant plant expansion, major manufacturing transformation, or complex production ramp-up.
* Strong knowledge of lithium-ion cell manufacturing or relevant advanced manufacturing technologies and processes.
* Broad understanding of manufacturing operations and the interdependencies among production, engineering, maintenance, quality, supply chain, materials, EHS, finance, and people.
* Strong financial and commercial acumen with experience managing operating budgets, forecasts, manufacturing costs, capital investments, productivity, and business performance.
* Demonstrated success building, leading, coaching, and developing high-performing leadership teams.
* Experience with workforce planning, organizational design, talent development, and leadership succession.
* Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, executive leadership, and cross-functional partners.
* Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Direct experience in lithium-ion cell manufacturing or large-scale battery manufacturing.
* Experience taking a newly constructed manufacturing facility through commissioning, production launch, volume ramp-up, and stabilized operations.
* Experience with highly automated manufacturing equipment and advanced manufacturing technologies.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, structured problem solving, operational excellence, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization or complex matrixed business environment.

**General Job Requirements**
----------------------------

* This position requires working in a plant/warehouse environment. Therefore, expect varying working conditions.

existing_roles.description:
**Overview**
------------

At Ford, you’ll work on ideas that matter, alongside passionate people who want to make a global impact. Together, we’re shaping the next era of transportation—grounded in purpose, driven by progress. Make your move.

* Job Type: Full time
* Work Type: Hybrid

 

We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.

 

Ford Energy is a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company dedicated to accelerating U.S. energy independence. Leveraging Ford’s century of manufacturing excellence and world-class battery energy storage systems (BESS) technology, Ford Energy designs, manufactures, and services grid-scale and commercial DC battery energy storage systems (BESS). Ford Energy is uniquely positioned to capture the growing demand for reliable, US-built energy storage systems. We are not just building batteries; we are building the infrastructure for the next generation of the American grid.

Why Ford Energy?

At Ford Energy, you have the backing of an industrial manufacturing powerhouse with the agility of a dedicated energy startup offering industry leading technology. We offer a competitive compensation package including performance-based bonuses, Ford vehicle discounts, and the opportunity to shape the energy strategy of one of the world's most iconic brands.

**In this position...**

The Senior Manager, Fulfillment & Logistics Operations is a senior leadership role accountable for the end-to-end fulfillment, logistics, and parts supply performance of the Project Operations & Performance value stream. This leader sets the direction for inventory and supply planning, parts replenishment, warehousing, distribution, and outbound product shipping, and owns the service, cost, and working capital outcomes of the network. The role also delivers the digital capabilities that give customers real-time visibility into parts inventory, order status, and shipment information, making fulfillment a differentiator in the customer experience. Partnering with Product Creation & Industrialization, Finance, Sales, and Procurement, this leader combines deep supply chain and logistics expertise with change leadership and the ability to build high-performing teams, delivering measurable business impact. [Scope: add annual logistics and inventory spend, number of facilities and 3PL partners, and team size.]

**What you'll do...**

**1. Strategy & Transformation**
 

* Own the fulfillment and logistics strategy across the Project Operations & Performance value stream, aligned with growth and customer experience goals.
* Lead transformation from concept to measurable results, including integration with Product Creation & Industrialization.
* Champion the Voice of Customer, resolve issues quickly, and incorporate insights into product, service, and fulfillment improvements.

**2. Parts Supply, Inventory & Warehousing**
 

* Lead end-to-end spare parts planning, inventory, and distribution, balancing availability, cost-to-serve, and working capital.
* Optimize inventory through segment-specific safety stock and reorder strategies, procurement controls, and clearance of slow-moving stock.
* Hold warehouse partners accountable for inventory accuracy, productivity, and safety.
* Partner with Finance to improve inventory velocity and the cash conversion cycle.

**3. Outbound Logistics & Delivery**
 

* Own delivery performance from factory release to customer or site, establishing service targets and driving perfect-order execution.
* Manage carrier, freight forwarder, and 3PL relationships, including contracts, rates, capacity, mode selection, and performance reviews.
* Ensure battery energy storage shipments meet hazardous materials and oversize/overweight transport requirements, including DOT, packaging, labeling, documentation, and permits.
* Coordinate production, shipping, installation, and site readiness across Sales, Manufacturing, Customer Project Teams, and Finance; resolve delays, damage claims, and exceptions.
* Reduce freight costs and lead times through route optimization, load consolidation, and standardized, system-integrated workflows.

**4. Digital Capabilities & Customer Visibility**
 

* Deliver customer self-service access to parts availability, consumption, order status, shipment tracking, and estimated delivery.
* Partner with IT, Product, and Sales to connect ERP, planning, warehouse, and carrier data through customer portals and API/EDI integrations.
* Provide proactive alerts for delays, backorders, and delivery changes; measure adoption, satisfaction, and reductions in order-status inquiries.
* Replace manual processes with automated workflows using SAP, advanced planning systems, and integrated data.

**5. Supplier & Production Alignment**
 

* Partner with Procurement to monitor Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier performance and mitigate material risks before they disrupt production.
* Align factory priorities with high-value customer orders and strategic inventory needs.

**6. Leadership, Performance & Continuous Improvement**
 

* Build and develop a high-performing fulfillment, logistics, and supply chain team.
* Present performance, risks, and investment cases to senior leadership and align cross-functional stakeholders.
* Own KPIs such as OTIF, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, backorders, fill rate, lead time, and cost-to-serve; quantify the financial and operational impact of improvements.
* Improve service and field performance through shorter repair cycles, higher first-time-fix rates, and greater product reliability.
* Lead change adoption and apply Lean and Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste and reduce fulfillment lead times.

**You'll have...**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Administration, or at least 10 years' of experience in a related field
* 8+ years of progressive experience in aftermarket operations, service supply chain, fulfillment, or logistics, including leading managers and multi-functional teams.
* Proven record of leading large-scale operational or digital transformation initiatives across multi-functional teams.
* Deep expertise in spare parts planning, inventory management, warehousing, distribution, and outbound logistics.
* Financial acumen, including budget ownership and working capital management.
* Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner with and present to stakeholders at all levels.
* Must be able to travel 50% as needed

**Even better, you'll have...**

* Master's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or APICS CPIM certification is a plus.
* Experience in the automotive or heavy equipment aftermarket/service industry.
* Experience delivering customer-facing digital capabilities, such as portals, order and shipment visibility tools, or API/EDI integrations.
* Experience in transportation, outbound logistics, or freight management, including hazardous materials or oversize/overweight shipping.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile).
* Experience working with Salesforce and/or SAP S4 HANA.
* Experience in high-mix, global manufacturing or consumer/industrial industries.

**Additional Information:**

Work Location: Dearborn or Kentucky (United States), but the company is willing to consider a hybrid modality

Required Travel: Up to 50% travel required

protected_roles.title: Director of Quality & Regulatory Compliance
protected_roles.description:
**Director of Quality & Regulatory Compliance**

**Miltope Corporation**

**Hope Hull, Al**

**Position Overview**

Miltope Corporation is seeking an experienced aerospace quality and regulatory compliance executive to lead the company's Quality organization and ensure continued compliance with applicable Department of War, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), and customer requirements.

This position has responsibility for the development, implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of the company's quality management systems supporting but not limited to:

* FAA Part 21 Production Approval operations.
* FAA Part 145 Certified Repair Station operations.
* EASA Part 145 Approved Maintenance Organization operations.

The Director of Quality & Regulatory Compliance will serve as the senior independent authority for quality assurance, regulatory compliance, and quality system effectiveness across production and repair station operations.

Reporting directly to the CEO/President, this individual will work closely with executive leadership, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Repair Station management to ensure that regulatory requirements are understood, implemented, monitored, and consistently maintained.

The successful candidate must possess the leadership capabilities to establish an effective quality culture while maintaining the technical knowledge and operational experience necessary to engage directly in regulatory matters, audits, investigations, and corrective action activities.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Regulatory Compliance and Quality System Leadership**

* Maintain overall responsibility for the effectiveness and compliance of Miltope's quality management systems supporting FAA Part 21 Production Approval and FAA/EASA Part 145 Repair Station operations.
* Ensure compliance with applicable FAA regulations, including 14 CFR Parts 21, 43, and 145, and applicable EASA Part-145 requirements.
* Maintain and oversee the implementation of applicable Quality Manuals, Repair Station Manuals, Quality Control Manuals, and associated procedures.
* Ensure that regulatory requirements, approved procedures, and customer-specific quality requirements are effectively communicated and implemented throughout the organization.
* Maintain awareness of regulatory changes and evaluate their impact on company operations, procedures, and approvals.
* Serve as the primary Quality organization representative in regulatory compliance matters and coordinate with designated Accountable Managers and regulatory authorities.
* Ensure that organizational responsibilities, delegated authorities, and quality reporting relationships are clearly defined and maintained.

**FAA and EASA Regulatory Oversight**

* Oversee the company's compliance with FAA Production Approval requirements, including organizational controls, production conformity, quality assurance, and product traceability.
* Oversee FAA Part 145 Repair Station quality control activities, ensuring compliance with the Repair Station Manual, Quality Control Manual, and applicable Operations Specifications.
* Ensure EASA Part-145 compliance monitoring requirements are effectively implemented and maintained.
* Ensure the designated EASA Compliance Monitoring Manager has the necessary independence, authority, resources, and organizational access to perform assigned responsibilities.
* Coordinate regulatory inspections, audits, surveillance activities, and responses to FAA and EASA findings.
* Maintain effective working relationships with FAA and EASA representatives and other applicable regulatory authorities.
* Ensure timely notification, investigation, and resolution of reportable quality and regulatory issues.

**Quality Assurance and Continuous Improvement**

* Establish and maintain an effective internal audit program covering production, repair station operations, suppliers, and supporting business functions.
* Ensure timely identification, documentation, investigation, and resolution of nonconformances and audit findings.
* Establish and maintain an effective corrective and preventive action (CAPA) process, including root cause analysis and verification of corrective action effectiveness.
* Monitor quality performance metrics, identify adverse trends, and drive improvement initiatives.
* Ensure appropriate controls for material acceptance, inspection, product conformity, nonconforming material, configuration management, calibration, and quality records.
* Oversee supplier quality management and ensure appropriate qualification, monitoring, and corrective action processes.
* Drive a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and regulatory compliance throughout the organization.

**Organizational Leadership and Executive Accountability**

* Report directly to the CEO/President and provide regular updates regarding regulatory compliance, quality performance, significant risks, and corrective action activities.
* Maintain independence from Manufacturing, Operations, and Repair Station production functions when performing quality oversight and compliance monitoring activities.
* Have authority to escalate significant quality and regulatory compliance concerns directly to executive leadership.
* Establish appropriate quality-related authority, including the ability to initiate product or maintenance holds and prevent release or return to service when applicable requirements have not been satisfied, consistent with approved procedures and delegated authority.
* Partner with functional leaders to ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained.
* Lead, develop, and mentor the Quality organization to ensure appropriate technical competency, staffing, and succession planning.
* Provide executive management with objective assessments of the effectiveness of the company's quality systems and regulatory compliance posture.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Aviation, or a related technical discipline preferred. Equivalent education and relevant aerospace industry experience will be considered.
* Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive experience in defense or aerospace quality assurance, regulatory compliance, manufacturing quality, or aviation maintenance quality.
* Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience managing a quality organization or regulatory compliance function.
* Demonstrated experience working within an FAA-regulated aerospace manufacturing organization holding a Part 21 Production Approval.
* Direct experience with FAA Part 145 Repair Station quality systems and regulatory requirements.
* Working knowledge of EASA Part-145 requirements, including compliance monitoring and organizational independence requirements.
* Demonstrated experience managing regulatory audits, responding to regulatory findings, and coordinating corrective actions with FAA, EASA, and customer representatives.
* Strong knowledge of aerospace quality management systems, including AS9100, AS9110, or equivalent standards.
* Demonstrated experience with root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action systems, supplier quality, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical organizational procedures and controls.
* Excellent leadership, communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to effectively communicate with executive leadership, regulatory authorities, customers, and employees at all organizational levels.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience overseeing multiple regulatory approvals or certifications within a single organization.
* Experience with both aerospace manufacturing and component repair/maintenance operations.
* Experience serving as or directly supporting a Part 21 Accountable Manager, FAA Part 145 Accountable Manager, or EASA Compliance Monitoring Manager.
* Experience with AS9100/AS9110 certification audits and aerospace customer audits.
* Experience implementing and maintaining risk-based quality systems and safety management processes.
* Experience managing quality organizations across multiple facilities or operating locations.

**Leadership Attributes**

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* Independence, integrity, and the willingness to address difficult quality and regulatory issues.
* The ability to influence executive leadership and operational management.
* Strong technical judgment and an understanding of aviation product safety and airworthiness.
* A proactive approach to identifying risks and preventing compliance issues rather than simply reacting to audit findings.
* The ability to balance regulatory requirements with practical business and operational considerations.
* A hands-on leadership style, with the willingness to engage in the details when necessary.

**Measures of Success**

Success in this position will be demonstrated by:

* Sustained compliance with FAA Part 21 Production Approval requirements.
* Continued compliance with FAA and EASA Part 145 Repair Station requirements.
* Successful completion of regulatory, customer, and third-party audits.
* Timely and effective resolution of audit findings and corrective actions.
* Effective quality system performance and reduction of recurring nonconformances.
* Strong organizational understanding of quality responsibilities and regulatory requirements.
* An independent, empowered Quality organization that supports business performance while protecting product conformity, airworthiness, and regulatory compliance.

Pay: $140,000.00 - $190,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* AD&D insurance
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Prescription drug insurance
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Wellness program

Application Question(s):

* How many year of experience do you have specifically in the rugged computing industry?
* How many years of experience do you specifically have in the field for which you have applied? Example: Engineering, Procurement, Electronic Assembly, Business Development

Work Location: In person

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

 

**Pratt & Whitne**y is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power systems and has been revolutionizing modern flight for over 100 years. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

Quality Director, Columbus Engine Center

**What You Will Do:**

* As the Quality Director for the Columbus Engine Center, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring a "quality-first" culture within a large, dynamic organization. You will lead strategic initiatives to enhance product safety, compliance, and operational excellence, while fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Your responsibilities will include:
* Providing strategic leadership for all Quality Assurance, Quality Control, and inspection activities across the Columbus Engine Center.
* Collaborating with Operations, Engineering, and Materials teams to ensure robust processes, effective change management, and prevention-based quality measures.
* Championing product safety through operational discipline and continuous improvement on the shop floor.
* Overseeing critical compliance programs, including training, records management, audits (internal, regulator, and customer), procedures, and major investigations.
* Monitoring and reporting on key quality metrics, developing action plans to achieve organizational goals.
* Ensuring adherence to AS9100, FAA, DCMA, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Leading root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives using CORE tools.
* Driving process capability improvements, defect reduction, and first-pass yield enhancements through data-driven decision-making.
* Managing nonconforming material, Material Review Board (MRB) processes, and risk assessments for critical aerospace components.

**Qualifications You Must Have**:

* Bachelor’s degree and 14 years of experience, or 12 years of experience with an Advanced degree.
* Experience in Quality Management within the Aerospace or other highly regulated manufacturing industry.
* Senior leadership or people management experience.
* Experience in Operations, Quality, or Engineering within the Aerospace manufacturing industry.

**Qualifications We Prefer**:

* 5+ years of experience in Operations Leadership.
* Experience leading organizations and other leaders.
* Aftermarket Aerospace / Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) experience.
* Familiarity with FAR-145 / CFR-145 Repair Station operations.
* Knowledge of FAA regulatory compliance.
* Background in Engineering.
* Airframe & Powerplant (A&P) Certification.
* Experience with SAP Quality systems.
* Understanding of AS9100 and Quality Management Systems (QMS).

protected_roles.title: Quality Management Director
protected_roles.description:
**Overview**

The Quality Management Director develops, implements, and maintains the hospital's Quality Management System in line with ISO 9001 and NIAHO standards. The director oversees the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program and keeps the hospital compliant with CMS Conditions of Participation and state requirements. The role leads survey and accreditation readiness, including mock surveys, tracers, and plans of correction. The director chairs or coordinates the quality committees, supervises the Quality and Compliance Associate, and monitors regulatory quality requirements. The director also oversees quality and patient safety data reporting, including dashboards and benchmarking, presented to the Medical Staff, Executive Leadership, and Board.

I. Minimum Qualifications:

A. Education:

1. Current licensure to practice as a Registered Professional Nurse in the State of Texas or equivalent degree in healthcare with a minimum of a baccalaureate degree. Master's degree in nursing, healthcare administration, quality management, or a related healthcare field preferred.

2. Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or higher) preferred.

3. Must have at least three (3) years of experience in management or quality improvement in an accredited acute care setting.

II. Knowledge and Skills:

1. Demonstrate knowledge and leadership skills to perform duties outlined in the job description

1. Must have strong knowledge of accrediting and regulatory agency requirements

2. Must have good problem solving, interpersonal communication and project management skills

3. Must be extremely detail-oriented with respect to documentation and communication

4. Able to read and interpret medical record documentation and hospital policies and procedures

5. Must have at a minimum proficient computer skills in using Microsoft computer programs (Word, Excel, PPT, etc.)

III. Personal/Physical Requirements:

1. Mental and physical health to meet demands of position

2. Must have respect for human dignity and cultural diversity

3. Demonstrates ability in use of verbal/written communication, and effectively communicate with patients, families, hospital staff, medical staff, and general public.

IV. Data Reporting Requirements:

1. Oversees and supports the data collection, validation, analysis, and submits required quality and patient safety data to regulatory, accrediting, and governmental agencies (e.g., CMS, Texas Health and Human Services, and the hospital's accrediting organization) within required timeframes, including all mandatory quality reporting program measures applicable to a rural hospital.

2. Ensures accuracy, completeness, and integrity of abstracted and reported data through routine audits, validation processes, and corrective action when discrepancies are identified.

3. Prepares and presents routine quality dashboards, scorecards, and trend analyses to the Quality Committee, Medical Staff, Executive Leadership, and Board of Directors, at least quarterly or as required.

4. Benchmarks hospital performance against state, regional, and national comparative data and identifies opportunities for improvement.

5. Maintains confidentiality of patient, and quality data in accordance with HIPAA, and hospital policy, and retains all reports and supporting documentation per record retention requirements.

V. Oversight Responsibilities:

1. Provides oversight of the hospital-wide Quality Management System, including the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, and ensures ongoing compliance with ISO 9001, NIAHO, CMS Conditions of Participation, and applicable state requirements.

2. Oversees survey and accreditation readiness, including mock surveys, tracer activities, and the development, implementation, and monitoring of plans of correction following internal or external surveys.

3. Oversees the work of the Quality and Compliance Associate.

4. Leads and monitors performance improvement projects, applying Lean Six Sigma and other process improvement methodologies, and tracks project outcomes and sustainability.

5. Chairs or coordinates quality committees, ensures committee minutes, action items, and follow-up are documented, and reports quality oversight activities to the Chief Executive Officer and the governing body.

Pay: From $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* AD&D insurance
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person
