protected_roles.description:
**Director of Quality**

**Location**

Carmel, IN • Memphis, TN • St. Louis, MO • Malden, MO • Peoria, IL • Other Illinois locations

**Leadership**

Directly manages at least two quality team members

**Travel**

Regular travel to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed

Weaver Popcorn is seeking a seasoned quality leader ready to step into a broader Director-level role. The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for food safety, quality assurance, regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and continuous improvement across the organization’s food manufacturing operations. This leader will strengthen and standardize quality systems, develop quality talent, and partner with plant and business leaders to ensure products consistently meet company, customer, certification, and regulatory requirements.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced food manufacturing quality professional who can set direction while remaining actively engaged with plant teams, audits, investigations, corrective actions, and day-to-day execution.

**HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?**
==============================

**Quality & Food Safety Leadership**
------------------------------------

* Develop and lead the company’s quality and food safety strategy, priorities, policies, procedures, and performance expectations across manufacturing locations.
* Ensure quality assurance and food safety programs are effectively implemented, maintained, verified, and continuously improved.
* Establish and oversee grain and popcorn quality standards from grower receipt and bulk storage through processing, bagging, and shipment, ensuring consistent quality controls throughout the supply chain.
* Provide visible leadership on the manufacturing floor through routine plant engagement, risk reviews, verification activities, and follow-up on quality concerns.
* Build a culture of accountability, prevention, compliance, and continuous improvement across Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and other partner functions.

**SQF, Audits & Regulatory Compliance**
---------------------------------------

* Lead and maintain SQF certification programs, including system ownership, audit preparation, certification readiness, corrective actions, and ongoing compliance.
* Plan, lead, and oversee internal, customer, certification, and regulatory audits of food manufacturing facilities.
* Ensure timely closure of audit findings, nonconformances, corrective and preventive actions, and related verification activities.
* Lead cross-functional Food Safety/HACCP, risk assessment, prerequisite program, and food quality teams.
* Monitor applicable food safety and quality requirements and translate them into practical operating standards and controls.
* Ensure effective quality controls for bulk grain storage, bin holds and releases, sampling, testing, and corn disposition prior to processing, including compliance with applicable phytosanitary requirements.

**Quality Management Systems**
------------------------------

* Own the effective use and continuous improvement of quality management system software, including document control, audits, corrective actions, training records, verification, and reporting.
* Standardize quality documentation, specifications, procedures, policies, records, and reporting across facilities.
* Use quality data, trend analysis, and leading and lagging indicators to identify risk, establish priorities, and improve performance.
* Ensure effective controls for ingredient sampling, product verification, environmental monitoring, sanitation verification, traceability, and other core quality programs.
* Provide oversight of corn testing and laboratory quality programs, including mycotoxin testing, internal and third-party sample testing, review of test results, and appropriate product disposition based on quality and food safety requirements.

**People Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership**
----------------------------------------------------

* Lead, coach, and develop a quality team of at least two direct reports, with potential for broader team responsibility as the function grows.
* Set clear goals, define accountabilities, assess performance, strengthen technical capability, and create development plans for quality team members.
* Partner with Plant Managers and Operations leaders to resolve quality issues without compromising food safety, customer requirements, or regulatory compliance.
* Establish and enforce hold/release and product disposition standards, with authority to stop processing or bagging operations and place grain, ingredients, or finished product on hold when food safety or quality requirements are not met.
* Partner with Sales and Customer Service to respond to customer documentation requests, audits, samples, complaints, and quality-related inquiries.
* Lead investigations into customer complaints, product or process deviations, and recurring issues; ensure root cause analysis and sustainable corrective action.
* Oversee nonconforming material, product holds, rework, release, and disposition processes, partnering with Operations and suppliers to ensure timely resolution and prevent recurrence.
* Provide clear quality updates, risk assessments, recommendations, and performance reporting to senior leadership and other decision-makers.

**WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?**
=============================

* Bachelor's degree in food science, Food Safety, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering, or related fields.
* 8–10+ years of progressive quality or food safety experience in the food manufacturing industry.
* At least 5 years of people-management experience, including progressive supervisory and manager-level responsibility.
* Proven leadership of SQF certification programs and successful food manufacturing audits.
* Demonstrated knowledge of food safety principles, quality assurance procedures and policies, HACCP-based programs, risk assessment, corrective action, and preventive controls.
* Experience leading internal, customer, certification, and/or regulatory audits across food manufacturing environments.
* Hands-on experience with quality management system software and electronic quality records.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence, develop teams, manage competing priorities, and drive consistent execution across locations.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate quality risk and technical requirements to operational and executive audiences.
* Ability to travel regularly to manufacturing facilities and business locations, as needed.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience in grain, corn, popcorn, milling, ingredient, or related agricultural processing.
* SQF Practitioner experience and formal training in HACCP, PCQI, internal auditing, root cause analysis, or preventive controls.
* Experience supporting multiple manufacturing sites or standardizing quality systems across locations.
* Experience with supplier quality, customer complaint management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recall readiness, and food defense programs.

**WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?**
================================

* Consistent audit and certification readiness across facilities.
* Stronger standardization and adoption of quality systems, procedures, and records.
* Timely, well-documented corrective action with verified effectiveness.
* Reduced recurrence of quality issues and customer complaints through disciplined root cause analysis.
* A capable, accountable quality team with clear goals and development plans.
* Credible, practical partnership with Operations and business leaders while maintaining independent quality judgment.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT & SCHEDULE**
===============================

This role operates across office and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Quality must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when operational, audit, customer, or food safety needs require support. Regular travel is expected based on business needs.

**HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?**
==============================

* Competitive compensation.
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**
================================

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

*The role responsibilities are many, various, and not limited to those written in this document*

protected_roles.title: Global Director of Quality
protected_roles.description:
**Lead Globally. Drive Innovation. Make an Impact.**

**Join Amphenol Alden and Make a Difference in Patient Care Worldwide!**

At **Amphenol Alden Products (AAP)**, what we do matters. Our medical cable assemblies and interconnect solutions support the advanced technologies healthcare professionals rely on every day. Behind every product is a patient, a family, and an opportunity to make a difference in someone's life.

With roots as a family business more than 90 years ago, Amphenol Alden combines a proud history and entrepreneurial spirit with the resources and opportunities of a global corporation. We are a growing organization that values innovation, teamwork, accountability, and the contributions of our employees.

We believe our people are the foundation of our success. That's why we offer competitive compensation, an outstanding benefits package, work/life balance, and opportunities for professional growth and development.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an experienced and strategic **Global Director of Quality** to lead and advance quality operations across four manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.

Reporting to AAP’s General Manager and serving as a member of the Leadership Team, this individual will establish and drive the global quality strategy, strengthen Quality Management Systems (QMS), and promote a culture of quality excellence and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

This is an opportunity to make a significant impact by developing high-performing global Quality teams, driving operational improvements, strengthening customer and supplier partnerships, and ensuring consistent quality standards across all manufacturing locations.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* **Global Quality Strategy:** Develop and execute global quality strategies, objectives, and initiatives that support business goals, product quality, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
* **Quality Management Systems:** Lead the development, implementation, standardization, and continuous improvement of Quality Management Systems across all facilities, ensuring compliance with ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable FDA requirements, customer specifications, and other relevant regulatory standards.
* **Executive Leadership:** Participate as a member of the Executive Leadership Team in establishing business strategies, operational objectives, and organizational improvement initiatives.
* **Quality Performance:** Establish and monitor global quality metrics, including customer complaints, internal and supplier defects, Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), corrective actions, and audit performance. Drive measurable improvements in quality and process capability.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and data-driven problem-solving methodologies to reduce defects, minimize waste, improve process consistency, and enhance overall operational performance.
* **Engineering and Operations Partnership:** Collaborate with Engineering and Operations to ensure effective quality planning, design and process FMEAs, risk assessments, process validation, and verification throughout the product lifecycle.
* **New Product Introduction:** Provide quality leadership for New Product Introduction (NPI) and manufacturing transfers, ensuring process capability, quality requirements, and customer expectations are met before production release.
* **Supplier Quality:** Partner with Global Supply Chain to develop and maintain a high-performing supplier base through supplier qualification, audits, performance monitoring, development, and corrective action programs.
* **Customer Quality:** Provide strategic leadership for customer quality initiatives, serving as the senior escalation point for significant quality concerns, customer audits, and corrective action resolution.
* **Audits and Regulatory Compliance:** Oversee internal and external quality audits, regulatory inspections, and management reviews, ensuring findings are addressed promptly and compliance is sustained.
* **Corrective and Preventive Action:** Strengthen global CAPA processes through effective root cause analysis, risk mitigation, and prevention of recurring quality issues.
* **Global Team Leadership:** Lead, mentor, and develop the global Quality organization, establishing clear expectations, accountability, talent development plans, and succession strategies.
* **Global Standardization:** Promote consistency and the sharing of best practices across manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, India, and China.
* **Executive Reporting:** Provide regular updates to executive leadership on global quality performance, emerging risks, customer satisfaction, and progress toward strategic quality objectives.

**Related Experience and Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, or a related technical or scientific discipline; Master's degree preferred.
* 10+ years of previous related experience and at least 5 years of experience managing individuals.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, FDA Quality System requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Management Systems and continuous improvement initiatives across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, CAPA, root cause analysis, risk management, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional teams, develop talent, and drive results in a global organization.

**Why Join Amphenol Alden?**

We believe great people deserve a great place to work. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your professional success, financial future, and overall well-being.

* Competitive salary and bonus opportunity.
* Hybrid work schedule.
* Excellent 401(k) retirement savings plan to help you plan for the future.
* Comprehensive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability, Health Savings Account (HSA), and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).
* Employee discounts and company-sponsored activities.
* Opportunities for professional growth and career development.
* The opportunity to lead a global organization and make a meaningful contribution to products that support patient care worldwide.

**Ready to Lead What's Next?**

If you are a strategic quality leader who thrives on building strong teams, solving complex challenges, and driving results across global operations, we'd love to hear from you!

**Join Amphenol Alden and help shape the future of our global operations while making a difference in patient care around the world.**

*Amphenol Alden Products is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

*Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship.*

protected_roles.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

**The Role**

Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.

This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

### **Requirements**

* You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
* You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
* You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
* You have taken a product through product safety certification
* You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
* You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so

### **Nice to haves**

* Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
* Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
* Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
* Experience with manufacturing execution systems

### **Benefits**

* **Fully employer-covered health insurance**, so you’re protected without the premium.
* **A managed 401(k)** to help you plan for the future.
* **Generous time off:** unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* **Regular in-office meals** and team social events throughout the year.

**Compensation**

The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

*Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.*

protected_roles.title: Head of Quality Control
protected_roles.description:
Department: Quality Assurance / Quality Control

Reports To: CEO / Executive Assistant

Location: On-site — Phoenix, Arizona Manufacturing Facility

Employment Type: Full-time

Industry Focus: Private-label OTC drugs, personal care, and nutraceuticals (dietary supplements)

Position Summary

The Head of Quality Assurance is the senior quality leader responsible for the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Specialty Formulations & Manufacturing’s Quality Management System (QMS) across all private-label product categories: over-the-counter (OTC) drugs, personal care and cosmetic products, and nutraceuticals / dietary supplements. This role owns regulatory readiness (FDA, state boards of pharmacy or health, and applicable international standards), batch release integrity, customer and brand-owner quality expectations, supplier quality, laboratory oversight, complaint and deviation systems, and inspection / audit performance.

The Head of QA is both a hands-on quality professional and a people leader. In a private-label environment, the position must balance speed-to-market and custom formulations with uncompromising compliance, documentation discipline, and brand-protection for client companies.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Own, maintain, and continually improve the site Quality Management System covering OTC drug CGMP (21 CFR 210/211), dietary supplement CGMP (21 CFR 111), and cosmetic / personal care good manufacturing practices (including 21 CFR 700 series and MoCRA-related requirements as applicable).
* Establish quality policy, quality objectives, management review cadence, and quality metrics (batch right-first-time, deviation rate, complaint rate, CAPA effectiveness, on-time release, audit findings).
* Author, approve, and control SOPs, specifications, master batch records, testing protocols, validation protocols, and quality agreements.
* Serve as primary quality contact for FDA inspections (drug, dietary supplement, and cosmetic), state inspections, customer audits, certification bodies, and third-party laboratories.
* Maintain inspection readiness at all times: documentation control, training files, equipment logs, environmental monitoring, stability programs, and reserve samples.
* Own FDA correspondence related to quality (483 responses, warning letter remediation, facility registration / listing support, product listing support as assigned).
* Final authority for batch disposition (release, reject, or quarantine) of OTC, personal care, and nutraceutical lots.
* Oversee in-process controls, finished-product testing, incoming raw material and component qualification, and certificate of analysis review.
* Ensure appropriate specifications exist for each private-label SKU, including customer-specific requirements captured in quality agreements and product technical files.
* Oversee environmental monitoring, water systems, cleaning validation / verification, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), and process validation appropriate to product risk. Deviations, Complaints, CAPA & Change Control
* Own deviation, OOS / OOT, nonconformance, customer complaint, and product quality complaint systems, including investigation quality and timely close-out.
* Lead CAPA from root-cause analysis through effectiveness checks.
* Administer change control for formulas, processes, equipment, suppliers, specifications, and labels that can affect product quality.
* Manage product hold, recall / market withdrawal readiness, and mock recall exercises. Supplier, Customer & Brand-Owner Quality
* Qualify and periodically requalify raw material, component, packaging, and contract laboratory suppliers; maintain approved supplier lists and quality agreements.
* Build a culture in which quality is owned on the floor—not only in the QA office—through training,
* Ensure cGMP, hygiene, documentation, and data-integrity training is current for all relevant employees and contractors.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemical Engineering, or a closely related scientific field. Advanced degree preferred.
* 2+ years of progressive quality experience in regulated manufacturing, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Direct experience with at least two of the three product categories: OTC drugs (21 CFR 210/211), dietary supplements (21 CFR 111), and personal care / cosmetics. Experience across all three is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated ownership of FDA inspection readiness and successful inspection outcomes.
* Proven ability to write and defend investigations, CAPAs, and regulatory responses.
* Working knowledge of USP, NSF or equivalent supplement standards, ISO 22716 (cosmetics GMP) or equivalent, and stability / shelf-life principles.
* Strong command of documentation systems, batch record review, and electronic or hybrid record control.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Familiarity with MoCRA, facility registration, product listing, and adverse event reporting for cosmetics.
* Familiarity with OTC monograph reform (CARES Act) and OTC labeling / Drug Facts requirements.
* Experience with dietary supplement identity testing, adulteration risk (e.g., spiked ingredients), and structure/function claim boundaries.

**Core Competencies**

* Intellectual honesty and backbone — willing to stop a batch or a shipment when the science or the record does not support release.
* Clear writing — SOPs, investigations, and FDA/customer responses that are precise, factual, and defensible.
* Operational partnership — works with production, purchasing, R&D / formulation, and sales without becoming a bottleneck or a rubber stamp.
* Risk-based thinking — applies controls commensurate with product risk (drug vs. cosmetic vs. supplement) rather than a one-size-fits-all bureaucracy.
* Teaching ability — raises the quality literacy of operators, formulators, and customer-facing staff.
* Confidentiality and professionalism with brand-owner formulas, claims, and audit findings.

**Working Conditions**

This is a hands-on, on-site role in a manufacturing environment. The Head of QA will spend time on the production floor, in the laboratory, in the warehouse, and in the quality office. The position requires the ability to review documents for extended periods, walk the facility, and respond to quality events, including during inspections. Some evening or weekend availability may be required during FDA inspections, customer audits, or critical batch investigations.

**Authority**

This position has independent authority to reject raw materials, halt production, withhold batch release, initiate product holds, and escalate quality risk directly to ownership. Quality decisions are not subordinate to

production schedule or sales commitments.

This job description outlines the general nature and essential functions of the role. It is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Duties may be added, removed, or modified to meet business and regulatory needs.

Pay: $31.25 - $40.87 per hour

Expected hours: 40.0 per week

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

protected_roles.title: Quality Improvement Director
protected_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Contentnea Health is a Community Health Center providing comprehensive medical, dental and behavioral health services for members of our communities in Greene, Pitt and Pamlico counties in eastern North Carolina.

**Job Summary**

Provides strategic leadership, oversight, and coordination of all organizational quality initiatives, including designing, implementing and evaluating quality programs to ensure delivery of safe, patient-centered, equitable, and efficient care, leads data-driven improvement efforts, and supports regulatory reporting and compliance with standards.

**Responsibilities and Duties**

* Oversees the Quality Improvement (QI) department activities.
 + Leads the development, implementation, and evaluation of the organization’s Quality Improvement Program.
 + Identifies opportunities to support QI efforts through evaluation, testing, and/or integration for electronic health record (EHR) functionality and other Heath Information and Technology (HIT) systems.
 + Summarizes and shares clinical quality data with the Board, key leadership, and staff to inform decision-making and priorities for improvement.
 + Champions the adoption of standardized best practices and lessons learned across disciplines and departments at the care team level and at the organizational level using communication tools, published workflows, staff meetings, events and trainings.
 + Facilitates QI Committee meetings and ensures documentation, follow-up, and progress tracking.
 + Establishes annual QI goals, work plans, and performance benchmarks aligned with strategic priorities.
 + Develops dashboards and data tools to share performance results with leadership and staff.
* Collaborates with and guides clinical care team members to establish QI processes through the organization.
 + Leads or participates in work teams related to QI and functions as a coach to support care team in building, fostering patient-centeredness and healthy patient outcomes.
 + Researches external organizations and participates in training opportunities, and works with partners, consultants and experts to guide QI efforts.
 + Assesses the need for and facilitates education, training, and technical assistance for staff to ensure compliance with QI efforts.
 + Uses existing data systems to identify areas in need of quality improvement across the organization.
* Oversees organizational data submission and sharing to external entities in collaboration with other departments as needed.
 + Follows regulation on data collection and reporting structure as defined by the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and health plan incentives.
 + Approaches changes to the EHR or other IT systems with consideration to data governance.
 + Monitors Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) requirements and the health center’s compliance.
 + Leads the annual FTCA deeming and redeeming application process and ensures all required evidence and documentation are completed and submitted accurately.
 + Ensures accurate and timely reporting of UDS clinical measures and other federal/state quality requirements.
 + Participates in HRSA review and response with organization leaders.
 + Acts as administrator for electronic Value-Based Care (VBC) and Quality Incentive Plans (QIP) platforms.
 + Partners with key leadership to determine participation priorities.
 + Oversees QI and clinical participation in contracted VBC and QIPs.
 + Monitors performance with VBC and incentive plans; shares performance data with key leadership.
* Ensures ongoing alignment with Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) standards, manages The National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) reporting and serves as PCMH project manager.
 + Leads annual submission of PCMH report to maintain recognition for each recognized site and maintains documentation and policies needed for audits, accreditation, and regulatory compliance.
 + Ensures all new hires are trained in PCMH processes, policies, and workflows, including care coordination, team-based care, access, patient experience and satisfaction.
 + Maintains current knowledge of NCQA/PCMH standards and serves as the subject matter expert. Analyzes and reviews processes, policies, and systems on an ongoing basis to ensure they are aligned with current and updated PCMH standards.
 + Uses data to drive continuous improvement in clinical quality, patient experience and cost/utilization outcomes.
 + Reports PCMH performance to leadership to inform resource allocation and prioritize performance improvement activities.
 + Coordinates PCMH improvement activities with staff and leadership.
* Provides overall management and direction to departmental staff.
 + Oversees the development and maintenance of the departmental budget; monitors ongoing budgetary compliance and addresses problems as needed.
 + Delegates departmental duties and responsibilities; participates in high priority special projects and activities.
 + Represents the department at all senior management meetings.
 + Prepares departmental company policies and procedures and conveys all senior management communications and directives.
 + Monitors departmental performance using company performance standards and addresses issues as needed.
 + Directs departmental performance and provides specific instructions on completion of tasks/responsibilities.
 + Prepares and conducts performance appraisals for immediate staff.
 + Conducts hiring, disciplinary, and termination procedures.

**Qualifications and Skills**

Bachelor Degree in Nursing. Current licensure as a Registered Nurse in good standing with the NC Board of Nursing. Possesses advanced understanding of quality improvement theory and quality methodology, evidence-based practice, state and national priorities for patient safety and population health as determined by HRSA, DHHS, and other entities, and regulatory, recognition and compliance standards, such as FTCA, PCMH, and HRSA. The ideal candidate will have progressive experience in leading quality improvement activities and in leading staff.

Join a company where innovation drives growth. At Alloy Precision Technologies, we combine cutting-edge manufacturing, skilled craftsmanship, and a customer-first mindset to deliver industry-leading solutions while providing employees opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

Alloy Precision Technologies

 

**SUMMARY:**

To provide strategic, operational, and day-to-day leadership to the manufacturing operations and manufacturing services function at Alloy Precision Technologies (APT) and to grow the business by increased productivity and profitability within a lean environment. Must be a proven leader who is capable of dealing with sometimes complex and difficult situations.

 

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Leads performance in the planning, coordination, and control of all manufacturing, supply chain, maintenance, production planning, and warehouse functions at APT and the personnel assigned to those functions.
* Establish both quality and efficiency in all production processes to meet performance objectives.
* Promote positive leadership to ensure safety goals and environmental programs for manufacturing operations.
* Direct, monitor, and provide specific feedback on production issues, opportunities, and delays. This will require a proactive approach to investigation and analysis, troubleshooting, and resolution.
* Design and implement on-time tracking systems to monitor manufacturing schedules and operations as necessary to ensure profitability, timely service, and product quality for strong customer service. Provide reports as requested or needed on all aspects of the manufacturing operation.
* Lead the development and implementation of improved operating methods via lean or other strategic manufacturing flow and business process systems and procedures to reduce costs, improve quality performance, and improve profitability.
* Develop effective lines of communication and cooperation between corporate departments and functions within areas of responsibility.
* Promote strong team-building skills. Demonstrate ability to mentor and motivate, as well as to delegate and empower others to succeed.
* Formulate annual operational objectives and programs governing manufacturing, service, and distribution.
* Performs described duties to meet or exceed Customer, AS9100, and regulatory requirements.
* Domestic and international travel may be required.
* Performs other duties assigned by the President and Chief Executive Officer.

 

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Directly supervises group leaders, supply chain, and production planning. Direct reports may be added or subtracted over time.
* Incumbent will carry out supervisory and managerial responsibilities by following APT organizational policies, applicable federal, state, and local laws. Responsibilities include: interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance: rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints, resolving problems, and career development.

 

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* BS in Operations Management, Industrial Management, Industrial Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with 10 plus years of manufacturing management experience. Experience in precision welding (tig, laser, brazing, and soldering), CNC and manual machining, and light assembly operations is a plus.
* Incumbent must have strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications. Experience with computer database systems, Visual Manufacturing, and the development of labor standards for cost structure is a plus. Must have a high level of energy, be results-oriented, confident, and have strong people skills. Must be able to establish and maintain a strong rapport and positive relationships with all levels of staff. Must be strategic in his/her orientation, proactive, persistent, and able to handle multiple projects and customers simultaneously, as well as work within a very fast-paced environment.
* Because the company runs at a very fast pace with multiple, rapidly changing priorities, the incumbent must be highly flexible, resilient, adaptable, and comfortable working in a dynamic organization with an evolving culture. Incumbent must enjoy a challenge, be passionate about his/her work, and commit to excellence and continuous improvement.
* Working knowledge of lean manufacturing methodologies required, Six Sigma is a plus.

protected_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities

protected_roles.title: Director, Quality
protected_roles.description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

We’re looking for a Director, Quality to lead quality strategy and execution across Oura’s global engineering organization and supply chain.

### **What You Will Do:**

* In this role, you will ensure that quality and reliability are designed into our products, components, suppliers, and manufacturing processes from concept through development, launch, ramp, and sustaining operations. You will lead a global team of quality professionals and partner closely with Product Development, Hardware, Software, Reliability, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Customer Experience, and external suppliers.
* You will connect customer and field needs to engineering requirements, component controls, supplier capability, manufacturing performance, and product reliability. Your team will help Oura identify risks early, make evidence-based decisions, prevent defects, and resolve complex issues with durable corrective actions.
* This is a broad, highly cross-functional leadership role for an experienced quality executive who can set strategy, develop talent, influence engineering and operations leaders, and engage deeply in both product and supply chain quality when needed.
* Set the quality strategy: Define Oura’s quality vision, operating model, standards, metrics, and priorities across product development, components, suppliers, manufacturing, reliability, and the field.
* Lead and develop a global quality organization: Build, mentor, and manage a high-performing team across product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, and sustaining quality.
* Embed quality across the product lifecycle: Establish effective quality gates and decision criteria from concept and architecture through EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, ramp, and sustaining.
* Partner with engineering and product leaders: Influence product architecture, design decisions, materials, specifications, interfaces, validation plans, and manufacturability to prevent quality and reliability issues.
* Strengthen component and supplier quality: Translate product requirements into component specifications, supplier quality requirements, qualification plans, control plans, inspection strategies, and process controls. Drive supplier capability and performance across the global supply chain.
* Drive manufacturing readiness and performance: Ensure production processes are validated and controlled, with appropriate PFMEA, process capability, measurement systems, yield targets, traceability, reaction plans, and continuous improvement mechanisms.
* Lead risk-based quality planning: Establish disciplined use of DFMEA, PFMEA, reliability planning, design reviews, tolerance analysis, GR&R, SPC, DOE, and risk-based verification and validation.
* Own complex problem solving: Lead containment, failure analysis, root-cause investigation, corrective action, preventive action, and verification of effectiveness for product, component, supplier, manufacturing, reliability, and field issues.
* Build strong field-quality feedback loops: Use warranty, returns, customer support, field failure, reliability, manufacturing, and supplier data to identify systemic risks and drive improvements that reduce member impact and cost of poor quality.
* Lead launch and ramp readiness: Review product and component qualification, supplier capability, manufacturing readiness, validation evidence, yield, open risks, reliability results, and corrective actions before launch and ramp decisions.
* Govern quality-related changes: Ensure design, material, component, supplier, process, software, and manufacturing changes are evaluated for quality and reliability impact and implemented consistently through ECR/ECN and change-control processes.
* Establish a data-driven quality operating system: Define leading and lagging indicators across development, suppliers, manufacturing, and the field. Improve data quality, traceability, dashboards, and escalation mechanisms.
* Drive continuous improvement: Reduce defects, escapes, returns, warranty claims, rework, scrap, and other sources of cost of poor quality while improving product reliability, supplier performance, and customer experience.
* Influence cross-functional decisions: Provide clear, risk-based recommendations when quality, schedule, cost, performance, capacity, and supply continuity priorities compete.
* Communicate with senior leadership: Present concise assessments of product risk, supplier and manufacturing performance, launch readiness, field quality, and improvement priorities.
* Build a culture of prevention and accountability: Make quality a shared responsibility across engineering and operations, with clear ownership for requirements, validation, supplier controls, manufacturing execution, and sustained performance.

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

### **What you'll bring**

* 15+ years of experience in product quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, operations quality, or a related engineering discipline, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading quality for complex, high-volume consumer electronics, wearable, medical-adjacent, or similarly reliability-sensitive products.
* Experience leading and developing teams across one or more of the following areas: product quality, component quality, supplier quality, manufacturing quality, reliability, program quality, or sustaining quality.
* A track record of establishing quality strategy, operating mechanisms, and measurable improvements from early product development through launch and sustaining.
* Strong understanding of product development, design verification and validation, component qualification, reliability engineering, supplier quality, manufacturing processes, and production ramp.
* Strong command of quality and problem-solving methods, including FMEA, 8D, CAPA, SPC, GR&R, DOE, root-cause analysis, control plans, and process capability.
* Experience using engineering, field, warranty, customer support, supplier, and manufacturing data to identify systemic risks and drive corrective action.
* Demonstrated ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, and executive leadership without relying solely on direct authority.
* Experience with engineering change control, supplier changes, component qualification, process validation, manufacturing readiness, or production quality improvement.
* Strong understanding of DFM/DFA, GD&T, Lean and Six Sigma principles, measurement systems, and quality management systems.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical risks into concise decisions and actions.
* A self-directed, pragmatic, and resilient leadership style, with a willingness to engage deeply in details while maintaining a strategic perspective.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, Systems, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field required; advanced degree or quality certification is a plus.
* Preferred qualifications
* Experience with both product quality and supplier or manufacturing quality, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively across both domains.
* Experience with batteries, electronics, sensors, RF systems, precision mechanics, adhesives, miniaturized assemblies, or other demanding product technologies.
* Experience leading quality for products that combine hardware, firmware, software, and cloud-enabled member experiences.
* Experience building or scaling quality management systems during rapid company growth.
* Familiarity with product safety, regulatory, compliance, traceability, and risk-management requirements relevant to wearable technology.
* Experience with supplier development, APQP, PPAP, SCAR processes, multi-source strategies, capacity expansion, or major manufacturing transitions.
* Experience working across multiple countries, engineering sites, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

### **Nice to have:**

* HW Experience
* Global distributor teams
* grown and org

### **Benefits**

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What we offer:

* Competitive salary and equity packages
* Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
* An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
* 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
* Paid sick leave and parental leave

Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Region 1 $226,000-$266,000
 
Region 2 $MIN- $MID
 
Region 3 $MIN- $MID

A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location.

We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI).

ŌURA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Individuals seeking employment at ŌURA are considered without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, protected family care or medical leave status, race, religion (including beliefs and practices or the absence thereof), sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

We will work to ensure individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.

Disclaimer: Beware of fake job offers!
 
We’ve been alerted to scammers posing as ŌURA recruiters, especially for remote roles. Please note:

* Our jobs are listed only on the ŌURA Careers page and trusted job boards.
* We will never ask for personal information like ID or payment for equipment upfront.
* Official offers are sent through Docusign after a verbal offer, not via text or email.

Stay cautious and protect your personal details.

To all recruitment agencies: ŌURA does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our jobs alias, ŌURA employees, or any other organization's location. ŌURA is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

**FLSA Status:** Exempt **Reports To:** President

**Job Type:** Non-Union **Amount of Travel Required:** Occasional

**Work Schedule:** Monday – Friday

Evenings, weekends, Holidays as needed. **Positions Supervised:** Production Staff

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Manufacturing executes the company operating plan within capital and operating budget parameters. The Director of Manufacturing works with the executive leadership team to develop strategies and objectives to maximize productivity and profitability. Analyzes production trends, forecasts future requirements, solve problems, motivates & develops employees.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

**Essential Functions Statement(s)**

 

* Improve operational efficiencies to reduce total production costs while meeting specific product volume needs
* Check and verify production records, handle questions or concerns of inventory shortages or overages and address problems with inventory control.
* Coordinate production schedules to meet sales demand. Adjust production as necessary to meet seasonal demands ahead of schedule.
* Ensure consistency in collective bargaining agreement and provide support during contract negotiations
* Effect necessary communication and motivation to staff. Monitors individual performance via observation and review of various productivity measures. Counsels and disciplines as necessary.
* Provides production required safety leadership and training and is responsible for improved safety performance
* Oversees all production planning and executing against demand signals.
* Oversees facility maintenance team, including Cap-Ex planning and execution.
* Provides input on new product development.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate health and food safety regulations and cleanliness, including audit preparation
* Manage customer complaint process.
* OSHA, Federal and State requirements are followed with the facility and equipment.
* Attends the Executive, Senior Management, and Safety Committee Meetings
* Maintain work area in a neat, orderly and sanitary manner.
* Correctly and promptly follow specified company procedures required for the appropriate handling of all.
* Emergency Responses and Safety practices.

**POSITION QUALIFICATIONS**

**Competency Statement(s)**

* Communication, Written – Ability to communicate in writing clearly and concisely.
* Collaboration - Collaborates positively to effectively build relationships with customers and co-workers to achieve company objectives and contribute to overall organizational success. Works effectively within a diverse environment. Exhibits a positive attitude and contributes to overall team success.
* Organized – Being organized or following a systematic method of performing a task.
* Communication, Oral – Ability to communicate effectively with others using the spoken word.
* Responsible – Ability to be held accountable or answerable for one’s conduct.
* Honesty / Integrity – Ability to be truthful and be seen as credible in the workplace.
* Accountability – Ability to accept responsibility and account for his/her actions.
* Reliability – The trait of being dependable and trustworthy.
* Friendly – Ability to exhibit a cheerful demeanor toward others.
* Customer Oriented – Ability to take care of the customer’s needs while following company procedures.

* Ability to work under stressful conditions

* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects in an organized and efficient manner
* Ability to respond to crisis situations in a calm and effective manner
* Ability to complete projects on schedule

North Greene Utilities is seeking a certified Level 3 Water Treatment Plant Manager to lead operations at our Level 3 water treatment production plant in Baileyton Tennessee. This is a key leadership role responsible for the full management of plant functions, regulatory compliance, and a small team of operators.

Position Overview

The Plant Manager oversees all day-to-day and long-term operations of NGU’s Level 3 water treatment plant. The position ensures continuous production of safe, high-quality water that meets or exceeds all Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards and guidance. The manager supervises, mentors, and develops a team of three subordinates while maintaining efficient, safe, and compliant plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage all plant functions and treatment processes to meet TDEC and EPA regulatory requirements and policy guidance.• Supervise, mentor, and train three subordinates. Two subordinates are expected to achieve Level 1 certification by mid-2027.• Develop, implement, and manage shift schedules to ensure continuous, reliable plant coverage.• Ensure compliance with all federal and state safety regulations and NGU safety protocols.• Conduct lifecycle and operational management of treatment infrastructure, including maintenance planning and capital needs.• Participate in daily stand-up meetings with the NGU management team.• Assist with HR requirements for subordinates, including ensuring compliance with company policies.• Monitor the health and welfare of subordinates.• Conduct biannual performance counseling for subordinates.• Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving operational requirements and tasks as directed by the Operations Supervisor and General Manager.• Maintain accurate records, reporting, and documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal management.

Qualifications

* Current Tennessee Level 3 Water Treatment Operator certification (required).• Proven experience in water treatment plant operations, preferably in a leadership or supervisory role.• Strong knowledge of TDEC and EPA drinking water regulations, treatment processes, and compliance requirements.• Ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet any additional job-related certifications or requirements (e.g., safety, drug and alcohol screening).• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.• Commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Compensation and Benefits

NGU offers very competitive wages, an IRA, health insurance, and dental coverage. Additional details on pay and benefits will be discussed with qualified candidates.

* Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills across all organizational levels

* Proficiency in leading change management initiatives

* Experience of working in a unionized environment.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
* Ability to travel up to 10-15% as required
* Experience maintaining safety programs and environmental compliance
* Excellent vendor and customer relationship management skills

**Compensation and Benefits**

The salary range estimated for this position based in Connecticut is $131,300.00–$205,000.00.

This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:

protected_roles.title: Director, Commercial Operations and Asset Management
protected_roles.description:
**SUMMARY:** The Director, Commercial Operations & Asset Management provides leadership over the operational execution and ongoing asset management of Rhyze’s Commercial lending platform. This role is accountable for establishing scalable, controlled processes across transaction closing, funding, participation, servicing and portfolio administration, while actively overseeing the performance, credit quality and risk profile of the commercial real estate loan portfolio.

The Director leads portfolio surveillance, borrower and property performance monitoring, covenant compliance, annual review coordination, delinquency management and the operational execution of workout and loss mitigation strategies. The position works closely with the Managing Director, Commercial; Capital Markets; and Legal, and coordinates with lead lenders, borrowers, servicing partners and participating credit unions as appropriate.

The successful candidate combines commercial real estate credit and asset management expertise with operational discipline, sound judgment, strong communication skills and a focus on scalable execution.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Commercial Portfolio & Asset Management**

· Lead portfolio surveillance and risk-based monitoring of commercial real estate loans, including payment performance, DSCR, net operating income, occupancy, rent rolls, leasing, borrower liquidity, maturities and concentration exposure.

· Oversee borrower and property financial reporting, covenant testing and compliance calendars; identify reporting deficiencies, covenant breaches, emerging risks and required follow-up.

· Coordinate annual and interim credit reviews, risk-rating assessments, watchlist management and action plans, with documented findings, ownership, deadlines and management escalation.

· Oversee collateral protection requirements, including insurance, property taxes, escrows, reserves, liens, property inspections, appraisals and other third-party assessments, in coordination with Servicing and Legal.

**Special Assets & Loss Mitigation**

· Identify and escalate delinquencies, maturity or covenant defaults and deteriorating credits; coordinate borrower outreach, collection strategies and remediation plans for criticized or classified assets.

· Evaluate requests for waivers, modifications, extensions, forbearances and other accommodations; develop supporting analysis and recommendations for authorized decision-makers.

· Coordinate workout and loss mitigation activities with Commercial leadership, Legal and external counsel, including enforcement, bankruptcy or foreclosure matters when applicable.

· Prepare required participant notices and approval packages; document borrower communications, decisions, conditions and deadlines, and monitor execution and performance under approved resolution plans.

**Commercial Operations & Servicing Oversight**

· Lead day-to-day Commercial operations with clear accountability, service standards, quality controls and escalation procedures across the loan lifecycle.

· Oversee transaction closing, funding, loan boarding and post-closing administration, including conditions, documentation, milestone tracking, data transfers and outstanding exceptions.

· Coordinate with internal teams, servicing partners and Capital Markets on participation administration, payment processing, reconciliations, escrows, reserves, borrower notices, payoffs, releases and related servicing matters.

· Ensure accurate implementation and recording of approved modifications, extensions and other post-closing actions, consistent with loan documents, participation agreements, delegated authority and applicable requirements.

**Operational Excellence, Reporting & Scalability**

· Provide timely loan-level and portfolio reporting to management and participating investors, including delinquencies, covenant exceptions, watchlist activity, material credit events and remediation progress.

· Serve as a central coordinator across Commercial, Capital Markets, Finance, Legal, servicing partners, lead lenders and participating credit unions on operational and portfolio matters.

· Develop and standardize procedures, controls, checklists, templates and reporting; identify opportunities for automation, integration and improved data quality to support scalable growth.

· Establish and monitor key performance indicators, including reporting compliance, review completion, exception aging, delinquency trends, watchlist resolution and transaction cycle times.

**Other**· Responsible for effective self/workload management. Demonstrates clear written and verbal communication skills. Promotes collaboration and a positive, professional work environment. Attends all position related meetings to ensure proper communication/planning occurs.

· Performs other related duties as assigned by the Managing Director

· Complies with all company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

· Care for non-public information (NPI) and ensuring that confidentiality of company, borrowers, and partner information is maintained.

· Responsible for contributing to a positive work environment and culture that represents the company values.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

· Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent professional experience considered.

· Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in commercial real estate lending, commercial credit administration, loan servicing, asset management, or a related field, with demonstrated experience managing commercial loan portfolios.

· Strong understanding of the end-to-end commercial lending lifecycle, including loan documentation, closing, funding, servicing, portfolio administration, and loan participations.

· Demonstrated expertise in commercial real estate asset management, including financial statement analysis, property performance monitoring, debt service coverage, covenant compliance, collateral valuation, and credit risk assessment.

· Experience identifying and managing problem loans, including delinquencies, covenant defaults, borrower accommodations, forbearances, modifications, workouts, and loss mitigation strategies.

· Strong knowledge of commercial loan servicing practices, including payment administration, escrow and reserve management, collateral protection, and post-closing compliance.

· Demonstrated ability to evaluate portfolio performance, identify emerging credit risks, develop actionable recommendations, and effectively communicate findings to management and other stakeholders.

· Experience establishing and improving operational processes, internal controls, reporting practices, and technology-enabled workflows to support efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

· Strong understanding of commercial lending regulatory requirements, credit policies, risk management practices, and financial institution governance.

· Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate cross-functional activities, and lead complex initiatives with a high degree of accountability and attention to detail.

· Excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage borrowers, lending partners, credit union executives, and internal stakeholders.

· Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently in an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented environment.

Pay: $165,000.00 - $185,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Remote

protected_roles.title: NPI Director North America - Solutions
protected_roles.description:
*Join the worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we* ***live different****,* ***play different****.*

We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.
* Contribute to global communities of practice and promote best-practice sharing across North American sites and with other regions.
* Foster a culture of customer focus, innovation, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications and Requirements:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, product development, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Significant leadership experience in NPI, product development, engineering, industrialization or complex program management within a multi-site manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, managing portfolios and leading major cross-functional product introductions.
* Strong commercial awareness and ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, operational risk and financial performance.
* Excellent communication, influencing and decision-making skills in an international and multicultural environment.
* Fluent professional English; additional languages are an advantage. Ability to travel across North America and internationally when required.

Benefits an **NPI Director North America – Solutions** can expect from Cartamundi:

* Competitive pay
* Climate controlled facility
* 401(k) with company match
* Health, dental, and vision insurance starting day one
* HSA (Health Savings Account) and FSA (Flexible Savings Account)
* Life insurance
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Paid time off
* Tuition reimbursement
* Employee discounts on daycare, gym memberships, travel, and much more

**Apply today and discover the magic of making a difference at Cartamundi!**

*Cartamundi does not discriminate based on race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities.* *This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. For more information on E-Verify, or if you believe that your employer has violated its E-Verify responsibilities, please contact DHS* *dhs.gov/e-verify**.*

*Candidates must be 18 years old to work for Cartamundi.*

*No agencies please. No sponsorship available.*

**About Cartamundi:**

At Cartamundi, we're all united by our common belief that world is better with play. Play is what keeps us going, and it always has been our greatest motivation. That's why we live different and play different. To us, it is not just an activity. It is a guiding mindset that reminds us to have fun, to be fair, to connect with people – across cultures and generations – and to embrace shared experiences.

We are a worldwide leader in playing cards and in “play” solutions.

Our owned brand portfolio includes a suite of heritage brands which go back as far as 1848, including global brands like Bicycle®, HRO®, Bee®, Copag®, Shuffle® and many locally loved brands. These brands combine craftsmanship with innovation as the basis for their continued relevance and positive contribution to the local communities that love and use these brands.

At Cartamundi, we have significant expertise in printing; our presses have been running since 1765. Today, our company has become the largest playing cards and board game manufacturer in the world and the trusted partner of leading toy companies. We make well-known brands such as Monopoly®, Uno®, Magic: The Gathering®, Guess Who ®, Pokémon®, Trivial Pursuit® every day.

As we look into the future and how entertainment evolves, we are bringing the digital world to the physical world and vice versa. We have a dedicated team of experts that is looking into future technologies, products, and applications that can get our consumers and communities to truly live different and play different.

We are still a family-owned company with headquarters in Belgium and have a global network of 16 manufacturing facilities, 6 design centers, 1 digital studio and 1 global R&D center
